concept.name: Classification
concept.definition: A supervised-learning task that maps inputs to one of a finite set of labels or estimates probabilities over those labels.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Fit a decision function or class-probability model on labeled training examples, choose any operating threshold on validation data, and evaluate held out outcomes.
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: A model estimates 0.68 probability that next-day return is positive and classifies it as up at a 0.60 threshold.

citations.section: Supervised learning, unsupervised learning, model selection, and inspection
